message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (120.65 K) | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | | **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ | | **Molecular shape** | Linear (diatomic) | | **Bond length (H–H)** | ~0.74 Å | | **Dipole moment** | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many other elements. | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; burns with a pale blue flame. | | **Isotopes** | • **Protium** (¹H) – most common, stable.
• **Deuterium** (²H or D) – one proton, one neutron; stable.
• **Tritium** (³H or T) – one proton, two neutrons; radioactive (half‑life ≈ 12.32 y). | | **Nuclear properties** | Tritium undergoes β⁻ decay to helium‑3. | | **Solubility** | Insoluble in water; soluble in liquid ammonia and liquid organic solvents. | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). | | **Uses** | • Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells).
• Chemical feedstock (ammonia, methanol).
• Metallurgy (reducing agent).
• Nuclear fusion research (deuterium–tritium reactions). | **Chemical Behavior Highlights** - **Oxidation states:** +1 (most common), –1 (hydride ions), 0 (molecular H₂). - **Acidity/Basicity:** Acts as a weak acid (forming hydronium, H₃O⁺) and a weak base (forming hydride, H⁻). - **Redox reactions:** Reduces metal oxides; oxidized to water or hydrogen peroxide in aqueous solutions. - **Combustion:** H₂ + ½ O₂ → H₂O (exothermic, releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹). These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, enabling its wide range of applications from industrial chemistry to energy storage and beyond.
